answer: Registration is a paced public forge that issues one key only after the applicant commits a unique cryptographic kernel—a high-entropy secret whose hash must not already appear on-ledger. The kernel is revealed under a delay, and a reused hash aborts minting and slashes a posted bond. Live voting power cannot fall below a published nadir of locked, unshared collateral; dipping below evicts the key. To operate N identities, an attacker must invent N unused kernels, wait through each forge delay, and maintain N separate nadir locks, so entropy, time, and capital scale with farm size.
